chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:

A man complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) of cracks in his hands and his legs, so he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Take a piece of cotton and put some frankincense oil in it and place it in your navel'. So Is'haq ibn Ammar said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Put the frankincense oil in the cotton and make it to be in his navel?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for you, O Is'haq, so pour the frankincense in your navel, for it is bigger (task)'. Ibn Udhaynah said, 'I met the man after that, so he informed me that he had done it once, so it went away from him'.
ai.seo_question: What is the remedy for cracked hands and legs according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s use of *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic medicine) and his awareness of individual physical constitutions, as seen in his humorous remark to Is'haq ibn Ammar regarding his large navel. It highlights the practical application of frankincense (*Luban*) for healing skin ailments, a practice rooted in both spiritual and medicinal traditions within Shia scholarship. The successful single application underscores the efficacy of this specific remedy when applied with precision.
